newsitem.title: YEMEN: Saudi minister due in Yemen for more border talks.
newsitem.headline: Saudi minister due in Yemen for more border talks.

text.p: Saudi Interior Minister Prince Nayef bin Abdul-Aziz is due to arrive in Yemen within the next two days for talks aimed at settling a 61-year-old border dispute, a Yemeni official said on Thursday.

"(Prince Nayef) will give Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh a letter from King Fahd dealing with the negotiations about the issue of borders between the two countries," the official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
Prince Nayef visited Yemen for border talks early this month, the latest in a series of moves to resolve the dispute.
Saleh said during the visit that a final settlement of the row was imminent and would be reached within weeks.

Yemen, one of the region's poorest countries, and oil-rich Saudi Arabia signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 to resolve the dispute. A joint committee looking into border demarcation has met dozens of times since then, but its work has moved at a slow pace, diplomats say.

Yemen has hinted in recent months it might resort to international arbitration. The two countries had several minor clashes in a border area potentially rich in oil and gas before signing the memorandum.
